title: Google Cloud IAM & Least-Privilege Governance (Roles, Service Accounts, Workload Identity)
author_notes: Effort tier: T4 (enterprise Google Cloud / identity / Gemini enablement).

Google Cloud Console / gcloud / Cloud Identity / Google Admin authored at exact detail from Google public docs; version- or preview-dependent capabilities (SCC tiers, BeyondCorp features, org-policy constraints, VPC-SC behaviors, Gemini Enterprise features) cited or flagged 'verify in your organization', never invented. IaC (Terraform / Cloud Foundation Toolkit) at the pattern level. Automation is Python (gcloud / Cloud Client Libraries) — no hardcoded credentials, no committed service-account keys, no secrets in code. No client names.
hook: Get Google Cloud access under least-privilege control
problem: Broad Owner grants, unmanaged service-account keys, and role sprawl are the most common Google Cloud security findings. This solution establishes Cloud IAM governance: a least-privilege role model (predefined vs custom), disciplined service-account and Workload Identity Federation use (kill exported keys), group-based access, org-policy IAM guardrails, and recurring access review — so who-can-do-what is intentional and auditable.
whats_inside: Solution Overview — the IAM model: principals, predefined vs custom roles, service accounts & Workload Identity Federation, group-based access, and the guardrails/review approach.
Requirements Guide — each prerequisite with how to verify/implement (Organization/hierarchy, org-admin access, groups source of truth, gcloud toolchain).

Implementation Guide — design the role model, replace SA keys with Workload Identity Federation, set group-based bindings at the right hierarchy level, apply IAM-restricting org policies, and stand up an access-review cadence — pilot-first.

5 Python tools — assessment/discovery, a configuration or provisioning helper, a validation/report generator, a policy/guardrail check, and a scope/config helper — authentic gcloud / Cloud Client Library automation (read-only or dry-run by default; no credentials or keys in code).
Validation gates (no broad Owner, no exported keys, bindings reviewed) plus Best Practices for durable least-privilege.
short: Establish Google Cloud IAM governance — least-privilege role model, Workload Identity Federation (no exported keys), group-based access, org-policy guardrails, and access review — so cloud access is intentional and auditable. Self-guided, tested, a fraction of consulting cost.

bottom_line: Google Cloud access under least-privilege control — role sprawl tamed, exported keys eliminated, bindings reviewed — intentional and auditable across the organization.
